questions.stem: The engine-room log is used to:
options: Record machinery readings, events and maintenance
Hold the passenger and crew lists
Keep the chart corrections up to date
Record the tides and the weather
questions.explanation: It documents operation and supports reporting if something goes wrong.

questions.stem: If the main engine stops unexpectedly you should first:
options: Shut off all electrical power at once
Tell the master and find the cause before a restart
Wait to see whether it restarts on its own
Restart immediately without checking anything at all
questions.explanation: Tell the bridge, check for obvious causes, and restart only if safe.

questions.stem: If a bump suggests the vessel has grounded, the engine-room operator should:
options: Continue normal operations and wait
Open sea valves to flood the bilge
Report to the master and check bilges, shaft and gland
Switch off the engine room lights
questions.explanation: Grounding can open the hull or damage the propeller and shaft.

questions.stem: In an engine-room fire the usual order is:
options: Increase fuel flow to burn the fire out
Alarm, stop fuel and air, get out, then the fixed system
Open all hatches to clear the smoke
Keep working until the smoke gets thick
questions.explanation: Raise the alarm, isolate the fuel and the air, close openings and account for everyone, then discharge the fixed system on the master's order. Adding fuel or opening hatches feeds the fire.

questions.stem: A Small Vessel Machinery Operator - Restricted certificate is valid:
options: Only on the passenger vessel named on it, under 750 kW
On any vessel in Canada with less than 750 kW of power
On any cargo vessel under 15 GT
On any tug in sheltered waters

questions.stem: You made a mistake in the engine-room log. The correct way to fix it is to:
options: Cover it with correction fluid and rewrite
Tear out the page and copy it out again
Erase it completely and write over it
Draw a single line through it, initial it, and correct it
questions.explanation: The original entry must stay readable because the log is a record that may be examined. Never erase or obscure it.

questions.stem: At handover, the outgoing watchkeeper should tell the relief:
options: Only the fuel used since the last watch
Nothing, because the log says it all
What is running, faults, work in progress and anything odd
Only the next meal time and the weather
questions.explanation: A good handover includes the state of the machinery, isolations, faults and orders. Leave only when the relief understands.

questions.stem: Which sequence best describes using your senses on a round?
options: Look only at the gauges and the alarm panel
Look for leaks, listen for noises, smell for heat, feel for vibration
Taste the oil, then listen to the bilge pump
Listen only to the alarm panel and log any alarms
questions.explanation: Rounds use sight, hearing, smell and touch. Many faults are noticed by senses before any alarm sounds.

questions.stem: The oil pressure of the running main engine falls to zero. You should:
options: Ignore it if the temperature is normal
Tell the bridge, stop the engine, and find the cause first
Speed the engine up to raise the pressure back to normal
Add more fuel to keep it running
questions.explanation: An engine can be destroyed in seconds without oil. Stop it, find the cause (level, leak, filter, pump or gauge) and do not restart until it is understood.

questions.stem: The coolant temperature is rising on a loaded engine. The most appropriate first step is to:
options: Increase speed to improve the water flow
Pour cold water on the cylinder head
Tell the bridge, reduce load, check coolant and sea water flow
Open the pressure cap at once to check
questions.explanation: Reduce the heat input and look for blocked sea-water flow, low coolant, slipping belts or a faulty thermostat. A hot cap can spray scalding coolant, and cold water can crack a hot engine.

questions.stem: Your engine overheated because the coolant is low. Before topping up you should:
options: Remove the thermostat permanently
Pour in cold water at once
Let it cool, find the leak, then refill slowly
Run at full speed to cool it down
questions.explanation: Adding cold liquid to a hot engine can crack the block or head. Find and fix the cause of the loss, refill, and bleed air out.

questions.stem: The high bilge alarm sounds at sea. After checking the alarm is real, you should:
options: Open all sea valves to equalise
Silence the alarm and carry on
Wait for the next round before checking it
Find the source, pump, and tell the bridge
questions.explanation: Locate the leak (hose, seacock, stern gland or hull), pump, isolate and report. If the water is rising faster than the pump can clear, tell the master at once.

questions.stem: The main engine stops without warning. The most appropriate action is to:
options: Crank repeatedly until it starts again
Close the fuel tank valves permanently
Say nothing until the next port
Tell the bridge, then check fuel and shutdowns before restarting
questions.explanation: The master needs to know quickly because the vessel may need to anchor or avoid danger. Check fuel valves, filters and alarms, and only restart once the cause is dealt with.
